why_v5: v4 was a candidate that named five knobs and never had 181 for three of them. v5 differs in two ways that matter. FIRST, the cross-host gate closed: 91004f7 composes the Xe algebra mask from the host's own bits instead of mining it per machine (d25efe6), which reversed 181's XE_TXN B0 failure, and the PPR master-mode device port (91004f7) made the PPR row worth measuring at all. SECOND, two features that did not exist when v4 was written - WP12's async pin-power CSV and WP5's CTA-per-node flat-XS kernel - turned out to be the two largest single wins of the whole campaign (-2.480 s and -0.913 s against a base of 16.658 s), and both are B0. The result is 11.189 s single-deck against MASTER's 27.2 s, and 981.7 cases/hour in batch against MASTER W16's 217.
arm_env_additions: APPENDED AFTER THE FREEZE, and recorded here because it changes the shape of a line this manifest quotes. The A2 outer-reduction design (docs/A2_OUTER_REDUCTION_DESIGN_20260902_KO.md Sec 2, Sec 5 item 6) found RASBERY_BICG_NMAX and RASBERY_BICG_EPS missing from src/Driver.h trajectory::kArmEnv. Both are read in the BICGCMFD constructor (src/BICGCMFD.cpp:74-81) into the inner BiCGSTAB budget _nmaxbicg (default 3) and its relative exit _epsbicg (default 0.1), and _nmaxbicg is the captured device graph's inner unroll -- so two runs that differ in it converge the flux to different depths and take different outer trajectories (this tree measured 6 -> 4 as i-SMR outers +6 %). They are now on the list. WHAT MOVES: the [RASBERY][TRAJECTORY] `env` object gains two more fields, printed as null for every run in this manifest because the reference line exports neither, and EVERY case key in the campaign moves once, because src/CaseKey.h's env half digests one line per name whether the name is set or not -- a cache MISS across the change, never a wrong hit. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: the trajectory `digest` and every outer count below it. The digest folds statepoints, outers, T/H steps and the bit patterns of efpd / k_eff / boron and reads no environment at all, so the confirmation_run PASS criteria stand exactly as written -- 238 prints 1f36e75dc00ed2b4 with 4377 outers and 181 prints 1afab8adb152bb44 with 4381 -- with two more nulls in the env object beside them.

benchmark_input.env_note: SELF-DESCRIBING ON PURPOSE. The last four knobs are now CODE DEFAULTS and an env that omitted them would resolve identically - but this file would then describe a binary instead of a run, and a reader could not tell an intended arm from an inherited one. There is also an operational reason: src/CaseKey.h digests the RAW env strings in kArmEnv order, so an unset knob and an explicit `1` are two different case keys for one arm. A controller that stopped exporting them after the flip would miss every cached case.
benchmark_input.env_note_absences: RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON stays DELIBERATELY ABSENT (single-deck default ON, and a baseline must exercise the default). RASBERY_STATEPOINT_TELEMETRY stays absent from the timing repeats. RASBERY_XE_FORMS stays absent and must NEVER be pinned: 0xadd was composed on 181 from 181's own mined 0xd3d, and pinning it on 238 overrides 238's correctly-mined shipped bits and moves the trajectory to 4374 outers even with XE_TXN off. Since d25efe6 the composition is automatic on both hosts and the pin is retired.
benchmark_input.env_measurement_rule: A wall or digest measured outside this env is not a measurement of this arm. The 2026-08-30 session produced a whole block of 'PPR is expensive' numbers (23.98 s / 4566 outers / digest 22b9a3187bfb4beb) whose only cause was a shell missing RASBERY_PC_MODE, RASBERY_PPR_MODE and RASBERY_OMP_THREADS. default_flip.what: Four knobs of the env above are now the binary's DEFAULT behaviour. Each keeps an explicit `=0` off switch, and each off arm is load-bearing rather than ceremonial.

RASBERY_GPU_CMFD_FUSE.off_switch: RASBERY_GPU_CMFD_FUSE=0 launches the reference kernels, which is what keeps mask 0 a LIVE reference rather than a memory of one
RASBERY_GPU_CMFD_FUSE.unparseable: falls back to the DEFAULT, not to 0. After the flip, silently dropping a typo to the reference path would look like a performance regression with no cause in any receipt.

not_flipped.RASBERY_GPU_CRAM: N1. The device depletion writes the isotope inventory the next statepoint reconstructs from, so it moves keff, critical boron and AO from the first statepoint onward - which is exactly why v5's digest and outer count differ from v3's. Per tools/promotion_gate.py an N1 feature is HOLD without a recorded project acceptance: a passed gate is not an approval.
not_flipped.RASBERY_GPU_PPR / RASBERY_GPU_PPR_GRAPH: B0 outside pin-derived datasets, N1 inside them (pin_power, summary/fqp, summary/frp). A feature that moves any published dataset does not become a default.
not_flipped.RASBERY_GPU_XFER_ELIDE / RASBERY_XFER_LE: not priced at all. An unpriced feature does not get a default, whatever its gate class.

default_flip.receipt_semantics: UNCHANGED, and this is the subtle part. trajectory::armEnvJson() prints the RAW exported string or `null` when unset - it does not resolve defaults, so that the receipt can never disagree with the solver about what the run was asked for. Consequence: an env-free v5 run prints `null` for RASBERY_GPU_FLATXS_CTA and RASBERY_GPU_XE_TXN where the explicit env prints "1". The `digest` field is unaffected, because it folds statepoints / outers / T-H steps / the bit patterns of efpd, k_eff and boron - and nothing from the environment. Both flipped knobs are B0, so an env-free run prints the SAME digest as the explicit-ON env by construction, on both hosts. The `case_key` IS affected (src/CaseKey.h digests the raw strings): unset and `1` are different keys for one arm, which is a cache MISS and never a wrong hit.
default_flip.contract: tools/test_v5_defaults_contract.py pins all four defaults, all four off switches, the three knobs that must stay opt-in, the raw set-vs-unset semantics of armEnvJson(), and the absence of any environment read from the digest fold - each with a negative control in both directions (back to opt-in, and forward to no-off-switch).
default_flip.confirmation_owed: ONE run per host, and it is the only thing in this file that has not been executed: the v5 env with the four flipped knobs REMOVED from the command line must reproduce the per-host digest and outer count below on a build of the flip commit. Both are B0 by three independent measurements each, so a failure would mean the flip itself was mis-wired rather than that the physics moved - which is why it is recorded here as owed rather than as blocking the freeze. See reproduce.confirmation_run.

flatxs_cta_kernel.counter_intuitive_finding: arm B's GPU BUSY FRACTION is LOWER than arm A's (3.9 pct vs 7.9 pct against the nsys-wrapped wall; 6.9 pct vs 13.3 pct against the real median). CTA cut total kernel time roughly in half while the wall moved much less, so the GPU now idles a LARGER share of the run. The bottleneck has moved off the kernels and onto host-side sync and the ~110K small cudaMemcpyAsync calls per run. That is where the next lever is, and it is not more kernel work.

throughput_baselines.control_discrepancy: THE ONE NUMBER THIS FREEZE DOES NOT EXPLAIN. The same-day control (old env, same procs/width/MPS share) measured 677.6 c/h against a historical reference of 877.6 c/h - 22.8 pct low, in the wrong direction, cause unknown. Five candidates were tested and four excluded outright: thermal/clock (no throttle flag active before or after), manifest (byte-identical job list), old build + old harness (386.8 c/h - reproduces the historical PLAN fields exactly and is far SLOWER), and solver_threads=1 forced on today's binary (304.1 c/h, the worst point of the sweep). The remaining untested cell is old binary + TODAY's policy (solver_threads=8 on 7cfe3a4).
throughput_baselines.which_baseline_to_quote: Against the same-day control, v5 batch is +44.9 pct (981.7 vs 677.6). Against the historical reference it is +11.9 pct (981.7 vs 877.6). Both are recorded. The same-day control is the more defensible comparison because it isolates the env change from whatever else drifted, but the historical number is not discarded, because nothing was found that explains it away.

open_items.warm_start_rejected: NOT an open item so much as a closed and negative one, recorded here so it is not re-proposed. WP10.2 warm-start was measured on 181 with the real parent/child pair (block 9): total outers INCREASED (8652 cold -> 8855 warm), which is the doc's own immediate-discard rule, and max|dk| landed at 2.36-2.40 pcm against a 1.905 pcm envelope and the tool's own 2 pcm tolerance. dppm (0.160-0.169) and dAO (0.0053) were comfortably inside. The mechanism is correct and fully wired - load:applied, provenance populated, flag-off prints no receipt at all - so this is a physics-acceptance rejection, not a defect. Warm-start stays OFF.
